meta.status: replication intervals for the approved DreamBench++ revisions; ORIDa excluded (on hold)
meta.resolved_rule: an interval is 'resolved' when it excludes 0 (lower > 0 or upper < 0)
meta.p_boot_two_sided: min(1, 2 * min(mean(d <= 0), mean(d >= 0))) over the paired replicates

primary_resampling.unit: subject = '<category>/<index>' of the DreamBench++ reference image (one cluster per reference image; all 7 methods x 9 prompts of a subject share it)
primary_resampling.procedure: per replicate: draw = rng.integers(0, n_clusters, size=n_clusters) over the sorted unique subjects; the replicate is the concatenation of all keys of each drawn subject, once per draw (a subject drawn k times contributes its keys k times)

secondary_resampling.unit: key (one generated image per method x subject x prompt)
secondary_resampling.procedure: index matrices rng.integers(0, n, size=(b, n)) in chunks of b = 250 replicates
secondary_resampling.caveat: treats the 63 keys of a subject, which share its reference image and mask, as independent

meta.pairing: within an analysis, every metric row uses the same index set per replicate; differences are computed replicate by replicate

statistics.alpha: Kd_o = mean over the two human rating groups g of interval Krippendorff alpha(row, g). Continuous rows are min-max normalised to [0, 1] on the rows of the resample (recomputed in every replicate) and compared with g / 4; 0-4 rubric rows (GPT-4o, GPT-4V) are used raw against raw g
statistics.rho: Spearman (average ranks) between the row and the mean of the two rating groups, ranks recomputed in every replicate
statistics.human_row: alpha(g1, g2) on raw ratings and Spearman(g1, g2)

meta.verification: cluster_ci.py self-tests (passed, SLURM 9155078): multiplicity of duplicated subjects, and alpha / rho / human ranks per replicate equal an independent recomputation on the materialised resample to 1e-9; all replicates finite
meta.scope: intervals describe the regenerated replication evaluation, not the printed main-table values

meta.canonical_rule: records on identical key sets, columns and statistic are the same comparison computed in different bootstrap runs; they differ only by Monte Carlo error. One is canonical, by source priority: filter| > strata| > stripping > boundary > table1_replication > table3_replication > table4_replication. Quote the canonical record everywhere. A single-run alternative needs a CPU rerun with one shared seed label (not done).
meta.seed_labels_differ_from_published_key_in: stripping and boundary keep the published key intervals (seed labels stripper_ablation, perturbation_dbpp_A, perturbation_dilation_vs_gpt4o) and take subject-cluster intervals from cluster_ci (cr_stripping|cluster, cr_boundary|cluster, cr_boundary_gpt4o|cluster)
